EXT.evidence: She energetically directs others to look at things (“look at the window,” “look at the paycheck amount”), announces her name on the window, and talks excitedly about her first paycheck.

AGR.evidence: She focuses on herself, tells others to look at her name and paycheck, and complains that FICA is taking all her money—coming off as boastful and self-centered rather than warm or generous.

CON.evidence: She emphasizes that she earned the paycheck and details specific tasks she did (“wiped tables,” “steamed milk”), indicating diligence and follow-through.

NEU.evidence: She reacts negatively and with frustration (“totally not worth it,” “FICA is getting all of my money”), showing emotional reactivity about the paycheck.

OPN.evidence: No clear signs of curiosity or unconventional thinking; asking who FICA is reflects confusion more than open-minded exploration.
